answer: An identity enters the ocean pool by locking a 55-credit canyon bond and taking work only from a randomly assigned client, checked by reef auditors. One client cannot serve many fakes: each assignment binds one client key to one identity key, and a mismatch burns the bond. The k-th fake pays 55 plus 8+0.03(k-1) in fees, so 1,000 fakes pay 55,000 in bonds and 22,985 in fees, 77,985 total. A rented-client ring fails: reef auditors reject a client signing for others, and shared keys void all linked bonds. An honest agent takes one assignment, delivers one work, and recovers the bond.
